chunks: Muḥammad ibn al-Fuḍayl narrated from Abū al-Ṣabbāḥ al-Kinānī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

If a bondwoman is sold while she has a husband, then the one who bought her has the choice: if he wishes, he may separate them, and if he wishes, he may leave her with him. But if he leaves her with him, then he has no right to separate them after he has consented.

He said: And if the male slave is sold, then if his master who bought him wishes to do the like of what the owner of the bondwoman did, then that belongs to him. But if he accepts, then he has no right to separate them after he has accepted.

key_terms.بِالْخِيَارِ: having the legal option or choice
key_terms.زَوْجٌ: husband; here, indicating an existing marriage
key_terms.سَلَّمَ: he accepted or yielded the matter
key_terms.فَرَّقَ بَيْنَهُمَا: separated the two spouses from one another

ai.seo_question: If a married slave or bondwoman is sold, can the new owner separate the spouses?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a married male or female slave when sold to a new master. The purchaser initially has the option to separate the spouses or leave the marriage intact, but once he consents to keep them together, he no longer has the right to separate them afterward.
